title: Pathomechanisms in neurogenic dysphagia due to Parkinson’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, inclusion body myositis and myasthenia gravis
summary:
Some neurological diseases can lead to swallowing disorders. Swallowing disorders are often treated with strengthening exercises. However, there is evidence that swallowing disorders are not always caused by muscle weakness. It is therefore important to examine whether the swallowing disorder is caused by e.g. spastic paresis, flaccid paresis or a movement disorder. This information may help to treat the respective problem in a more targeted manner.
Flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES), an instrumental swallowing assessment, may help here. With a FEES, neurologists and/or speech therapists can detect signs of the swallowing disorder and give treatment recommendations. Initial studies show that a FEES examination can also be used to observe a movement disorder or flaccid paresis during swallowing. In the present study, FEES data from patients with Parkinson's disease (PD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), inclusion body myositis (IBM) or myasthenia gravis (MG) will be used to examine whether these findings of an observation of movement disorders or paralysis can be confirmed by an FEES.  
A movement disorder or paralysis may also affect speech. Therefore, in addition to swallowing, speech will be examined using the Bogenhausen Dysarthria Scales (BoDyS, Ziegler et al., 2018). The BoDyS can be used to determine whether a neurologically induced acquired speech disorder is present and to what extent and how severely speech is impaired. This allows further conclusions to be drawn about spastic or flaccid paralysis or a movement disorder.   
In this study, it is assumed that signs of spastic paralysis, flaccid paralysis or a movement disorder appear during swallowing. Furthermore, it is assumed that the signs of spastic paresis, flaccid paresis or a movement disorder will mostly be concordant for speech and swallowing in the respective clinical pictures. 
A total of 40 patients with PD, ALS, IBM and MG will be examined, i.e. ten patients per disease.
conditions: Neurogenic dysphagia due to PD, ALS, IBM and MG.

interventions.name: In patients with PD, ALS, IBM or MG, a brief logopedic history, a FEES and the BoDyS (Ziegler et al., 2018) are carried out once.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
There is an indication for a FEES. For this study, there is an indication for a FEES if dysphagia is suspected by the attending physician or if the diagnosis of dysphagia has already been confirmed by a clinical swallowing examination (KSU), FEES or videofluoroscopy (VFSS) and a re-evaluation of swallowing is indicated.
Exclusion criteria:
-  Contraindications for FEES (e.g. unstable general condition, acute cardiac symptoms, vomiting)
- Stress tolerance/attention < 60 min 
- Other neurological diseases that can cause dysphagia/dysarthria
- Mutism
